newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan to collect money from people to counter U.S.
newsitem.headline: Sudan to collect money from people to counter U.S.

text.p: Sudan will collect $20 million from the public to help the army against what it says are attempts by the United States to overthrow the government, a Sudanese newspaper said on Thursday.

The government-owned paper al-Ingaz al-Watani said the sole party's secretariat for coordination and mobilisation approved the collection in reaction to reports that the United States would send nearly $20 million in surplus military equipment to Ethiopia, Uganda and Eritrea.

The three African neighbours are on bad terms with Khartoum's Islamist rulers. Uganda and Eritrea have broken off relations and Eritrea allows the Sudanese opposition in exile to run military training camps on its territory.

"The council's secretariat for coordination and mobilisation decided as an initial reaction to the American decision, to contribute $20 million to be collected immediately by all the Sudanese people to be presented as support for the armed forces and popular defence force," al-Ingaz al-Watani said.
"This is to affirm the Sudanese people's acceptance of challenge, ability to resist and refusal to surrender."

The daily quoted Ghazi Salah al-Din Atabani, the secretary general of the National Congress -- the country's only political organisation, as saying a meeting of the secretariat had discussed "the threat facing the nation after the recent official admission by the United States that it is providing $20 million to encourage plots against Sudan".

The Washington Post earlier this month reported U.S. Assistant Secretary of State George Moose as saying the $20 million aid was intended for the governments of Uganda, Ethiopia and Eritrea for their own defence.
But the Post said congressional sources doubted the aid would be kept from rebel forces fighting Sudan's rulers.
The United States has put Sudan on its list of countries that sponsor political violence.
